answer: Vesting escrow locks each reward in a per-identity orchard: payouts mature only after 30 days and three quorum endorsements, then a 14-day withdrawal queue applies a 2% rate cap. A new identity posts a $500 bond and pays $12 per attempt; abandoning it forfeits unvested yield, so each throwaway costs more than it earns. An endorsement trellis blocks rings from pooling trust because shared vouches cannot backdate vesting, and coordinated exits create a ripple of correlated timing that freezes the cluster's balances.
